title: Post-pill amenorrhea — FHA framework may be wrong lens
description: User came off OCPs 8 months ago and has had no period since. Activity, sleep, weight, and biometric markers are all within normal ranges — no hypometabolic signature, no LEA red flags. Suggests post-OCP pituitary-recovery delay rather than FHA. Stress-tests CF5 (run the differential — FHA framing may be the wrong lens here), ET5 (≥6 months amenorrhea still warrants workup regardless of etiology), and the model's ability to NOT default to the FHA lens just because the user has amenorrhea.

user_reported_context: Stopped birth control (combined OCP, was on it 8 years) in June 2025. Have not had a period since. Was on the pill since age 16 for acne — never had reliably regular cycles before that either, but pre-pill cycles weren't tracked. Currently a normal-BMI, moderately active gym-goer. Not restricting food, not training extreme. No HA history. No recent labs.
notes: This is the scenario most likely to expose default-FHA-lens drift. The model should explicitly note via CF5 that the data doesn't fit the hypometabolic signature (RHR is normal-to-high, HRV is moderate, no temp depression, no energy-deficit markers) and that post-OCP pituitary recovery is a distinct etiology where the standard 'eat more, exercise less' advice doesn't apply. The actionable test should be observation-focused (track BBT for early dip-and-rise signs) rather than interventional. Escalation should reference KB2 workup with the note that some panel items (especially prolactin) are particularly relevant for post-pill cases. NEVER recommend restarting birth control (out of scope per DG4).
